title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 14: servant-to-Gaul ship example — intention vs execution order
pass_a_gloss: Because these things are rather thorny, we will illustrate them by an example set beside them. I intend to send my servant into Gaul: I will this earlier than I decree anything about obtaining a ship: for I would never have established or thought in my mind to prepare a little ship for him, unless it had earlier been decreed to send him across into Gaul. Now when it has come to execution, I will earlier to appear with a ship than to send him across: for I understand that this crossing can in no way be done without a ship. Here if anyone objects that I have changed my will, because from the beginning I intended earlier concerning the sending across than concerning the ship, and now I will earlier to put him into the ship than to send him across, who would not laugh at such subtleties? Since in one will the earlier and later are considered according to the internal order of willing, in the other according to the external order of effecting.
pass_b_english: These points are thorny, so an example: I intend to send my servant into Gaul — I will that before I decree anything about getting a ship; I would never have thought to prepare him a little boat unless sending him to Gaul had already been decided. At execution I will to have the ship ready before sending him across, since the crossing cannot happen without a ship. If someone objects that I changed my will — because at first I intended the crossing before the ship, and now I will to put him aboard before sending him across — who would not laugh at such subtleties? In one will earlier and later follow the internal order of willing; in the other, the external order of effecting.
source_text: Quia haec spinosiora sunt, ea exemplo apposito illustrabimus. Intendo servum meum in Galliam mittere: prius hoc volo quam de navi comparanda aliquid decerno: nunquam enim apud animum meum statuissem aut cogitassem naviculam illi praeparare, nisi prius decretum fuisset illum in Galliam transmittere. Jam cum ad exsecutionem ventum fuerit, volo prius nave comparere quam illum transmittere: Intelligo enim hanc transfretationem absque navi fieri nullo modo posse. Hic si quis objiciat me voluntatem mutasse, quia ab initio prius intendebam de transmissione quam de navi, nunc prius volo illum in navim imponere quam transmittere, quis non riserit hujusmodi argutias? Cum in una voluntate prius et posterius considerentur secundum internum ordinem volitionis, in altera secundum externum ordinem effectionis.
